gap: No result ChatGPT got states how the two call systems work or what that requires of the wearer: on the AeroClip 2, 2 VPUs (voice pickup units) pick up the wearer's own voice instead of filtering out the noise around it, rated for 80+ dB surroundings, and its mic sits where the battery housing meets the C-bridge, so Anker says each bud must be on its correct ear and not swapped left/right during calls; the C50i's 2 AI mics only filter background noise.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Soundcore AeroClip 2 and C50i product pages, ChatGPT's three answers, our current Dealectric page, Soundcore's AeroClip vs AeroClip 2 blog (2026-09-28) and Expert Reviews. The cited AeroClip 2 product page already says '4 mics and 2 VPUs isolate your voice instead of filtering noises … 80+ db', and ChatGPT's answers repeat '4 mics + 2 voice pickup units'. So the voice-isolation idea is already partly on rival pages. None of those pages say where the mic sits, that the buds must be on the correct ears for calls, that dual-device connection can't be turned on during a call, or that LDAC only applies on Android (Expert Reviews heard it on a Pixel, not an iPhone). Our page calls the VPUs 'bone-conduction mics', which isn't Anker's term, and lists LDAC with no note that it's Android-only.
decides: This supports the pick ChatGPT already made rather than changing it. The AeroClip 2's extra $100–130 mostly pays for a different way of picking up the voice (VPUs on Anker's Thus chip), not for better music. iPhone owners get AAC, not LDAC, so for them the music argument mostly goes away and calls are nearly the only reason to pay more. Anyone who doesn't take calls in loud places should buy the C50i.
